Susan,

Thanks — got the milestone sheet. Attaching a first-pass "MAP Mosaic" that attempts to surface owner-level milestones, gating dependencies (MSA -> DPA -> Order Form), and suggested review windows. High level summary below and a proposed 30-min sync to lock dates.

Summary / recommendations:
- Split the legal review into two parallel lanes: (1) MSA commercial terms (pricing, liabilities, payment), (2) DPA/security attachments (data flows, processors). That lets commercial and security reviews run concurrently and shortens end-to-end.
- Suggested review windows: 10 business days for first commercial review, 8 business days for DPA/security (assuming SOC2 evidence available).
- Critical path: Signed MSA with payment terms -> Order form signoff -> DPA executed (can be after order form if the customer accepts the DPA as an attachment and agrees on a remediation plan). We'll call this a staged execution if needed.
- Acceptance gating: pilot acceptance criteria (test dataset, latency SLA, data retention) should be owned by Biomedix Product and Redwood Solutions Engineering.

Proposed next steps:
- I propose a 30-min sync on Wed May 6, 10:00 AM PT to walk the MAP Mosaic and confirm dates. Marissa will own the MAP artifact maintenance and share the DocuSign link / HubSpot milestone after we lock dates.

I've attached: Redwood_MAP_Mosaic_v1.xlsx, MSA_DPA_Blueprint.pdf (redline playbook). Also requesting your SOC2 and pen test artifacts if available (the SOC2 Report speeds the DPA review).

If that works, I'll calendar the sync and include Karthik for legal sequencing.

Laura / team,

Thanks for the draft. A few legal sequencing notes to make the MAP operational from our side:

1) Dual-track review (recommended)
   - Commercial MSA: prioritize core commercial terms (scope, payment, liability caps). We can accept a condensed redline window of 10 business days for initial review; please flag any non-starters within 3 business days.
   - DPA/security: treat the DPA as an attached schedule; security can complete a substantive review in ~8 business days if SOC2 and encryption details are provided up front. If SOC2 is missing, add 7 business days for evidence collection.

2) Staged execution approach
   - We can agree to a staged signing model for pilot customers: sign MSA + Order Form to enable invoicing and seat provisioning; complete DPA execution within a defined SLA (e.g., 30 calendar days post-order) with agreed interim controls. This avoids blocking technical kickoff.

3) Redlines and version control
   - Requesting that Biomedix mark MSA redlines in a single document and DPA redlines in a separate schedule. We'll track versions in the HubSpot attachment and use DocuSign when both parties agree.

4) Required artifacts (please confirm delivery owners/dates)
   - SOC2 Type II report (2025) — helps compress DPA review window
   - Pen test summary or attestation
   - Data flow diagram for pilot dataset (who has access, retention, export controls)

I'll be available to join the Wed May 6 sync. If Biomedix prefers a different close cadence, we can adjust but the dual-track + staged signing approach is the fastest practical route to pilot kickoff.
